ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Toy check that a one-step generator recovers token correlations lost by set prediction
PROPOSAL: Build a synthetic teacher: an autoregressive model over sequences of 8 tokens from a codebook of 32 entries, trained on a dataset with strong pairwise correlations, in the spirit of the two-sample example (0,0) and (1,1). Train a one-step generator mapping Gaussian noise to the full sequence by matching the teacher's output distribution, with two seeds. Compare sequence-level total variation distance and pairwise token statistics on 50,000 samples.
CONTROLS: Set prediction with two tokens per step; a one-step generator that factorizes over positions; the teacher sampled token by token as the reference; a run with noise dimension 8 instead of 64.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The distribution-matching generator should keep pairwise statistics within a few percent of the teacher, while the factorized generator should collapse toward a uniform mixture. If both match the teacher, the toy is too easy to discriminate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Synthetic teacher study of one-step generators by sequence length, codebook size and correlation strength
PROPOSAL: Build synthetic teachers: autoregressive models over sequences of 4, 8 or 16 tokens from codebooks of 16, 32 or 64 entries, trained on data with strong pairwise correlations. Train a one-step generator from Gaussian noise by matching the teacher's output distribution, using three seeds per configuration. Compare sequence-level total variation distance and pairwise token statistics on 50,000 samples and give a table for every configuration.
CONTROLS: Set prediction with two tokens per step; a position-factorized one-step generator; the teacher sampled token by token as reference; noise dimensions of 8 and 64; a teacher with weak correlations.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The distribution-matching generator should keep pairwise statistics near the teacher's across configurations, while the factorized generator collapses toward a uniform mixture. Gaps may widen with the longest sequences and the biggest codebook.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reverse-divergence training of a one-step generator through relaxed token samples
PROPOSAL: Take a pretrained class-conditional LlamaGen model with a 16x16 token grid as the frozen teacher. A transformer generator receives a noise vector and class label and outputs logits for all 256 positions at once. Draw relaxed token samples with a Gumbel-softmax, score them under the teacher's next-token distributions, and minimize reverse divergence plus an entropy term. Train on 100 ImageNet classes with three seeds, and evaluate FID on 10,000 samples.
CONTROLS: DD1 distillation at the same iteration count; a generator trained with cross-entropy on teacher samples alone; a run without the entropy term to expose mode collapse.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The relaxed objective should land within about 1.5 FID of the teacher's sampling and beat a sample-regression generator at equal iterations. Without the entropy term the generator is likely to collapse onto a few modes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Straight relaxation versus score-function gradients for one-step token generators
PROPOSAL: Distill a frozen LlamaGen teacher with a 16x16 token grid into a one-step transformer generator taking noise and a class label. Compare two gradient estimators for the teacher-scored objective: Gumbel-softmax relaxations at low, middle and high temperatures, and a score-function estimator with a learned baseline. Train on 100 ImageNet classes with two seeds and report FID, precision and recall on 10,000 samples after 50 and 100 epochs.
CONTROLS: DD1 at the same epoch count; a sample-regression generator trained on teacher samples; each estimator without the entropy term; a variant that freezes the first half of the generator.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The relaxed estimator at the middle temperature should come within about 1.5 FID of the teacher and beat sample regression. The score-function estimator may show higher variance and slower convergence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy estimation inside distribution matching for a one-step generator
PROPOSAL: In a compact setting with a 4x4 token grid and a 256-entry codebook, train single-step generators against a small autoregressive teacher fitted to MNIST tokens. Compare two ways of controlling diversity in the matching objective: a batch-level nearest-neighbor entropy estimate and a per-position entropy bonus from the generator's logits. Use three seeds and 20 epochs, and measure token-sequence likelihood under the teacher, number of distinct generated digits, and FID against the teacher's samples.
CONTROLS: A generator with no diversity term; samples from the teacher as an upper reference; the same pair of terms with the weight changed by a factor of 4.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: Both entropy controls should keep distinct-digit coverage near the teacher's, and the nearest-neighbor estimate should score a little higher on teacher likelihood. With no diversity term the generator is likely to concentrate on a handful of digit classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diversity control in distribution matching for token grids and codebook sizes
PROPOSAL: Train one-step generators against autoregressive teachers fitted to MNIST and SVHN tokens with grids of 4x4 and 8x8 and two codebook sizes. Compare three diversity controls in the matching objective: a batch-level nearest-neighbor entropy estimate, a per-position entropy bonus, and a coverage penalty. Use two seeds and measure teacher likelihood, number of distinct generated classes, and FID against teacher samples for all configurations.
CONTROLS: A generator with no diversity term; teacher samples as an upper reference; each control with its weight changed by a factor of 4; a teacher trained on half the data.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: All three controls should keep class coverage near the teacher's, and the nearest-neighbor estimate should score a little higher on teacher likelihood. With no diversity term the generator is likely to concentrate on a few classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-step class-conditional ImageNet generation distilled from a frozen autoregressive teacher
PROPOSAL: Use LlamaGen-B at 256x256 resolution as the frozen teacher and train a single-step generator that maps a Gaussian latent and a class label to all 256 tokens in one pass. The objective matches the teacher's output distribution using its next-token probabilities, with no predefined noise-to-token mapping. Train on ImageNet for 300 epochs with two seeds and report FID, Inception score, precision and recall on 50,000 samples.
CONTROLS: DD1 at the same training length; the teacher with ordinary token-by-token sampling; a generator initialized randomly versus from the teacher's weights; speculative decoding for the step-count comparison.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The generator should reach FID within about 2 points of the teacher after a single step and clearly beat DD1 at equal training length. Gains may shrink if the matching loss is noisy early in training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Class-conditional distillation of two autoregressive teachers into one-step generators
PROPOSAL: Distill LlamaGen-B and a VAR teacher, both at 256x256 resolution, into one-step generators that map a Gaussian latent and a class label to all tokens in a single forward pass. The objective matches the teacher's output distribution using next-token probabilities. Train on ImageNet with three seeds per teacher and report FID, Inception score, precision and recall on 50,000 samples at three training lengths.
CONTROLS: DD1 per training length; the teacher with ordinary token-by-token sampling; random versus teacher-weight initialization; speculative decoding as a step-count reference.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Both generators should land within about 2 FID of their teachers in one step and clearly beat DD1 at equal training length. The VAR teacher may be harder, since its coarse-to-fine token order differs from raster order.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a bigger teacher with a stronger tokenizer into one step
PROPOSAL: Distill the 775M LlamaGen-XXL teacher at 384x384 resolution into a single-step generator with a Gaussian prior, matching the teacher's output distribution from its next-token probabilities. Train on ImageNet with three seeds. Evaluate FID, precision and recall on 50,000 samples, and measure wall-clock latency per image on a single accelerator against 576-step teacher sampling.
CONTROLS: DD1 trained to the same iteration count; the teacher sampled with classifier-free guidance at its tuned scale; a one-step generator without guidance distillation.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The one-step generator should reach an FID within roughly 2.5 of the guided teacher and run at least 100 times faster per image. Guidance may be the hardest part to absorb, leaving a visible diversity gap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generator width and guidance scale for one-step distillation of a bigger teacher
PROPOSAL: Distill the 775M LlamaGen-XXL teacher at 384x384 resolution into one-step generators of three widths with a Gaussian prior, matching the teacher's output distribution from its next-token probabilities. Train on ImageNet with two seeds, evaluating FID, precision and recall on 50,000 samples at five guidance scales, and measure per-image latency against 576-step teacher sampling.
CONTROLS: DD1 at the same iteration count for each width; the teacher with guidance at its tuned scale; generators without guidance distillation per width.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The middle-width generator should reach an FID within roughly 2.5 of the guided teacher at 100 times lower latency. Wider generators may add little, and guidance remains the hardest part to absorb.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distribution-matching versus adversarial training for one-step token generation
PROPOSAL: Compare two ways to train a one-step generator from a frozen LlamaGen-B teacher at 256x256 resolution: matching the teacher's output distribution with its next-token probabilities, and training a discriminator in the codebook embedding space against teacher samples. Use 100 ImageNet classes and two seeds, and report FID, precision, recall and training stability across 5 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: DD1 at equal iterations; a generator trained with both objectives mixed; adversarial training with the discriminator also fed teacher likelihoods; the teacher's own sampling as reference.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The likelihood-matching generator should reach lower FID and a smoother training curve than the adversarial one. The adversarial model may recover higher precision but lose recall, with unstable checkpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Objective comparison for one-step token generators with a mixing-weight study
PROPOSAL: Compare three ways to train one-step generators from a frozen LlamaGen-B teacher at 256x256 resolution: matching the teacher's output distribution with its next-token probabilities, training a discriminator in codebook embedding space against teacher samples, and a mixture of the two at low, middle and high weights. Use 100 ImageNet classes and three seeds, and report FID, precision, recall and stability over 10 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: DD1 at equal iterations; the matching objective alone per weight; a discriminator also fed teacher likelihoods; the teacher's sampling as reference.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The likelihood-matching objective should reach lower FID and a smoother curve than the adversarial one, with a small mixing weight adding precision. The adversarial model may lose recall and show unstable checkpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prior dimension and prior shape in one-step token generation, on a compact teacher
PROPOSAL: Use a small autoregressive teacher over a 4x4 grid of tokens from a 128-entry codebook fitted to CIFAR-10 tokens. Train one-step generators whose latent is Gaussian with dimension 16 or 128, and compare against a uniform latent, matching the teacher's output distribution. Use two seeds and 20 epochs, and measure teacher likelihood, FID against teacher samples, and how often distinct latents yield identical token sequences.
CONTROLS: A generator with the latent concatenated to class embeddings; a deterministic generator with no latent; the teacher sampled token by token as reference.
COST: 16
PREDICTION: A Gaussian latent of dimension 128 should give lower FID than dimension 16 and fewer duplicate sequences. A uniform prior should perform about as well as the Gaussian prior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent design study for one-step generators matched to compact teachers
PROPOSAL: Use small autoregressive teachers over 4x4 and 8x8 grids of tokens from two codebook sizes fitted to CIFAR-10 tokens. Train one-step generators whose latent is Gaussian with dimension 16, 64 or 256, or uniform, matching the teacher's output distribution. Use three seeds and measure teacher likelihood, FID against teacher samples, and how often distinct latents yield identical token sequences in each setting.
CONTROLS: Latent concatenated to class embeddings; a deterministic generator with no latent; the teacher sampled token by token as reference; a prior with correlated coordinates.
COST: 16
PREDICTION: A Gaussian latent of dimension 256 should give lower FID than dimension 16 and fewer duplicate sequences. Uniform and Gaussian priors may perform about the same, since the generator can reshape either.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-step text-to-image generation distilled from an autoregressive teacher
PROPOSAL: Distill a frozen text-conditioned autoregressive image model producing 1024 tokens per image, such as Lumina-mGPT at 512x512, into a one-step generator mapping a Gaussian latent and a prompt embedding to all tokens. Match the teacher's output distribution through its next-token probabilities. Train on 2 million image-caption pairs with three seeds, and report FID, CLIP score and GenEval on 30,000 prompts.
CONTROLS: DD1-style distillation extended to text prompts; the teacher with token-by-token sampling; speculative decoding for step counts; a one-step generator trained only on teacher samples.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The generator should keep CLIP score within 1 point and GenEval within 5 points of the teacher at a thousandfold cut in steps. Prompts with counted objects may expose the loss of correlations between distant tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt-scale analysis of one-step text-to-image distillation from an autoregressive teacher
PROPOSAL: Distill a frozen text-conditioned autoregressive image model producing 1024 tokens per image, such as Lumina-mGPT at 512x512, into one-step generators trained on three data sizes, up to 8 million image-caption pairs. The generator maps a Gaussian latent and a prompt embedding to all tokens, matching the teacher's output distribution through its next-token probabilities. Use two seeds and report FID, CLIP score and GenEval on 30,000 prompts.
CONTROLS: DD1-style distillation extended to text prompts per data size; token-by-token teacher sampling; speculative decoding for step counts; a generator trained only on teacher samples.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The generator should keep CLIP score within 1 point and GenEval within 5 points of the teacher at a thousandfold cut in steps, with data size adding little past 2 million pairs. Prompts with counted objects may expose lost long-range correlations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training speed of likelihood-matching generators compared with fitting a fixed mapping
PROPOSAL: Measure how quickly each approach reaches a target quality with a frozen LlamaGen-B teacher at 256x256 resolution. One generator fits the noise-to-token mapping built by flow matching, as DD1 does, and the other matches the teacher's output distribution directly with its next-token probabilities. Train both on ImageNet with two seeds and log FID at 10 intervals, plus iterations needed to reach an FID of 8.
CONTROLS: DD1 as the fixed-mapping baseline with its published schedule; the matching generator with a warm start from the teacher's weights; a cold start from random weights.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: The matching generator should reach the target FID in roughly half the iterations of the fixed-mapping model. If the matching loss is noisy, early checkpoints could trail the fixed mapping.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Convergence study of mapping-free distillation by batch size, learning rate and initialization
PROPOSAL: Measure how quickly each approach reaches a target quality with a frozen LlamaGen-B teacher at 256x256 resolution. Train the DD1 generator and the likelihood-matching generator on ImageNet with batch sizes of 256 and 1024, three learning rates and warm or cold starts, using three seeds, log FID at 10 intervals, and record the iterations needed to reach an FID of 8.
CONTROLS: DD1 with its published schedule at each batch size; the matching generator with warm and cold starts; a run using half the teacher's depth for the generator.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: The matching generator should reach the target FID in roughly half the iterations of the fixed-mapping model at each batch size. Cold starts at the high learning rate may diverge, and early checkpoints could trail the fixed mapping.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Zero-shot editing through latent inversion of a one-step token generator
PROPOSAL: Ask whether a generator trained by distribution matching can be steered after training, which a fixed noise-to-data mapping may rule out. Tokenize 200 ImageNet validation images and recover a latent for each by gradient descent. Edit by interpolating latents and by optimizing toward a text direction in CLIP space, with three seeds, measuring reconstruction error and class consistency of the edits.
CONTROLS: The DD1 generator inverted by the same procedure; inversion without the latent prior term; token-space inpainting with the teacher as reference.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Latents from the matching generator should reconstruct images with lower token error than DD1 inversion, and interpolations should stay class-consistent in most cases. Inversion could fail for rare classes where the generator has low coverage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Encoder, optimization and masked-completion benchmark for one-step token generators
PROPOSAL: Probe what a distribution-matched one-step generator offers beyond sampling. Tokenize 2,000 ImageNet validation images and recover latents for them in two ways: gradient descent at 3 step budgets, and a trained encoder network. Run latent interpolation, CLIP-direction optimization and masked completion, with two seeds, scoring token reconstruction error and whether the class survives each edit.
CONTROLS: DD1's generator put through the same recovery steps; recovery with the prior term removed; teacher-based masked completion as reference; a random-latent control.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Latents from the matching generator should reconstruct images with lower token error than DD1 inversion, and interpolations should stay class-consistent in most cases. Rare classes with low generator coverage may resist inversion.
